source.text: Ἀποθέμενοι οὖν πᾶσαν κακίαν καὶ πάντα δόλον καὶ ὑποκρίσεις καὶ φθόνους καὶ πάσας καταλαλιάς, ὡς ἀρτιγέννητα βρέφη τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γάλα ἐπιποθήσατε, ἵνα ἐν αὐτῷ αὐξηθῆτε εἰς σωτηρίαν, εἰ ἐγεύσασθε ὅτι χρηστὸς ὁ κύριος.

records.literal_gloss: Having put off therefore all malice and all deceit and hypocrisies and envies and all evil speakings, \v 2 as newborn infants the spiritual pure milk long for, so that by it you may grow into salvation, \v 3 if you tasted that kind [is] the Lord.

en.L: Having put off, therefore, all malice and all deceit and hypocrisies and envies and all slanders, \v 2 like newborn infants long for the pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up into salvation, \v 3 if you have tasted that the Lord [is] kind.
en.B: So rid yourselves of all malice and every kind of deceit, of pretending and envy and all slander. \v 2 Like newborn babies, crave the pure milk of God's word, so that by it you may grow up into salvation, \v 3 now that you have tasted that the Lord is kind.
en.R: So get rid of every kind of evil. Stop lying and pretending. Stop being jealous and saying bad things about others. \v 2 Newborn babies cry for milk. In the same way, you should long for the pure milk of God's word, which feeds your spirit. It will help you grow until you receive the salvation God has for you. \v 3 For you have already tasted how kind the Lord is.

es.L: Habiéndo{{plural_you:se|os}} quitado, pues, toda malicia y todo engaño e hipocresías y envidias y todas [las] calumnias, \v 2 como niños recién nacidos {{plural_you:deseen|desead}} la leche espiritual pura, para que por ella {{plural_you:crezcan|crezcáis}} hacia la salvación, \v 3 si {{plural_you:han|habéis}} probado que el Señor [es] bondadoso.
es.B: Así que {{plural_you:despójense|despojaos}} de toda malicia y de toda clase de engaño, de la hipocresía, de la envidia y de toda calumnia. \v 2 Como niños recién nacidos, {{plural_you:anhelen|anhelad}} la leche pura de la palabra de Dios, para que por ella {{plural_you:crezcan|crezcáis}} hasta alcanzar la salvación, \v 3 ya que {{plural_you:han|habéis}} probado que el Señor es bondadoso.
es.R: Por eso, {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} toda clase de maldad. No {{plural_you:mientan|mintáis}} ni {{plural_you:finjan|finjáis}}. No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} envidia ni {{plural_you:hablen|habléis}} mal de los demás. \v 2 Los bebés recién nacidos lloran pidiendo leche. Así también {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} desear la leche pura de la palabra de Dios, que alimenta el espíritu. Ella {{plural_you:los|os}} ayudará a crecer hasta que {{plural_you:reciban|recibáis}} la salvación que Dios tiene para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. \v 3 Porque ya {{plural_you:han|habéis}} probado cuán bondadoso es el Señor.

sw.L: Basi, mkiisha kuvua ubaya wote na udanganyifu wote na unafiki na wivu na usengenyaji wote, \v 2 kama vichanga vilivyozaliwa karibuni yatamanini maziwa ya kiroho yasiyochanganywa, ili kwa hayo mkue kufikia wokovu, \v 3 ikiwa mmeonja kwamba Bwana [ni] mwema.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo vueni ubaya wote na kila aina ya udanganyifu, unafiki, wivu na usengenyaji wote. \v 2 Kama vichanga vilivyozaliwa karibuni, tamanini sana maziwa safi ya neno la Mungu, ili kwa hayo mkue mpaka mfikie wokovu, \v 3 kwa kuwa mmeonja kwamba Bwana ni mwema.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo achaneni na kila aina ya ubaya. Acheni kusema uongo na kujifanya. Acheni wivu na kuwasema wengine vibaya. \v 2 Watoto wachanga hulilia maziwa. Vivyo hivyo, mnapaswa kutamani maziwa safi ya neno la Mungu, yanayolisha roho zenu. Yatawasaidia kukua mpaka mpokee wokovu ambao Mungu amewaandalia. \v 3 Kwa maana mmekwisha kuonja jinsi Bwana alivyo mwema.

decisions.choice: having put off: a participle that shares the force of the command "long for"
alternatives: a separate step that must come first
decisions.reason: Ἀποθέμενοι is the language of taking off clothes (compare Ephesians 4:22; Colossians 3:8). It hangs on the command ἐπιποθήσατε ("long for"), so it is part of what the readers are told to do. οὖν ("therefore") ties it to 1:22-25: they have been born again through the living word, so they must put off what destroys love for one another.

decisions.choice: five sins of speech and attitude that break up a community
decisions.reason: κακίαν is ill will, δόλον deceit or trickery, ὑποκρίσεις acting a part, φθόνους envy, and καταλαλιάς speaking against others behind their backs. Each one damages the love among believers that 1:22 commands.

decisions.choice: spiritual milk, which comes through the word of God
decisions.reason: λογικὸν can mean "spiritual" (as in Romans 12:1) or "belonging to the word" (λόγος). Coming straight after 1:23-25, where the readers are born again through the living word of God, the milk is most likely that word, and it is milk that feeds the spirit rather than the body. Both ideas may be meant.

decisions.choice: pure: unmixed, with nothing false in it
decisions.reason: ἄδολον was used of goods that were not watered down. It plays on δόλον ("deceit") in verse 1: they put away deceit and long for milk with no deceit in it.

decisions.choice: grow up into salvation: grow until salvation is complete at the end
alternatives: grow because you are already saved
decisions.reason: σωτηρίαν in 1 Peter is mostly the full salvation still to be revealed in the last time (1:5, 1:9). The readers are already born again (1:23), and the milk makes them grow toward that goal.

decisions.choice: Psalm 34:9, where "the Lord" is the divine name; here it means Jesus
decisions.reason: The words echo Psalm 34:9 (Greek Psalm 33:9), "taste and see that the Lord is good". In the Hebrew psalm "the Lord" is the divine name YHWH. Peter applies it to Jesus, for the next verse goes on "to whom you come, a living stone". Psalm 34 is quoted again in 3:10-12. χρηστὸς ("kind, good") sounds almost the same as Christos, and the play may be intended.

decisions.choice: if: since, as is true
decisions.reason: εἰ here assumes the condition is met: the readers have tasted the Lord's kindness. The sentence does not question their experience.

decisions.choice: the pure milk of God's word (B); the pure milk of God's word, which feeds your spirit (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the milk as the word (m3). Literal keeps "spiritual". A footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: now that you have tasted (B); For you have already tasted (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "if" assumes (m7); "if" alone would sound doubtful in modern English. Literal keeps "if".

decisions.choice: Stop lying and pretending. Stop being jealous and saying bad things about others.
alternatives: put away all malice and all deceit and hypocrisy and envy and all slander
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the list into short commands with plain words for each sin (m2).

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Peter writes to the churches in the plural throughout the letter. As in Paul's letters, each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain).

decisions.choice: Habiéndo{{plural_you:se|os}} quitado
decisions.reason: "Quitarse" is what one does with clothes, so Literal keeps the picture of taking off old clothing that the meaning decision describes. Balanced "despojarse" keeps it too.

decisions.choice: mkiisha kuvua (L); vueni (B)
decisions.reason: "Kuvua" is to take off clothes, so Literal and Balanced keep the picture the meaning decision describes. Readable says "achaneni na" (have done with), as the English Readable says "get rid of".

source.text: Πρὸς ὃν προσερχόμενοι, λίθον ζῶντα, ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων μὲν ἀποδεδοκιμασμένον παρὰ δὲ θεῷ ἐκλεκτὸν ἔντιμον καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡς λίθοι ζῶντες οἰκοδομεῖσθε οἶκος πνευματικὸς εἰς ἱεράτευμα ἅγιον, ἀνενέγκαι πνευματικὰς θυσίας εὐπροσδέκτους θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: To whom coming, a stone living, by men indeed rejected but with God chosen, precious, \v 5 also yourselves as stones living are being built a house spiritual for a priesthood holy, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ;

en.L: Coming to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, a living stone, rejected indeed by {{gender:people|men}} but chosen [and] precious with God, \v 5 you yourselves also, as living stones, are being built up [as] a spiritual house, for a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: You come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the living stone that {{gender:people|men}} rejected as worthless but God chose and prizes. \v 5 And you yourselves, as living stones, are being built up as a house for the Spirit, to serve as a holy priesthood and to offer, through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, spiritual sacrifices that God gladly accepts.
en.R: You come to the Lord Jesus. He is the living stone. {{gender:People|Men}} decided {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was worthless and rejected {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but God chose {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and to God {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is precious. \v 5 You are like living stones too. God is building you together into a house where {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit lives. There you serve as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy priests. Through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} you offer God spiritual sacrifices that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is glad to accept.

es.L: Acercándo{{plural_you:se|os}} a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, piedra viva, rechazada ciertamente por {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}} pero elegida [y] preciosa ante Dios, \v 5 también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos, como piedras vivas, {{plural_you:son|sois}} edificados [como] casa espiritual, para un sacerdocio santo, para ofrecer sacrificios espirituales aceptables a Dios por medio de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes se acercan|Vosotros os acercáis}} a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, la piedra viva que {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}} desecharon como inútil, pero que Dios eligió y tiene en gran estima. \v 5 También {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos, como piedras vivas, {{plural_you:están|estáis}} siendo edificados como una casa para el Espíritu, para servir como sacerdocio santo y ofrecer, por medio de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, sacrificios espirituales que Dios acepta con agrado.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes vienen|Vosotros venís}} al Señor Jesús. Él es la piedra viva. {{gender:Los seres humanos|Los hombres}} decidieron que no valía nada y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} rechazaron, pero Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} eligió, y para Dios es precioso. \v 5 {{plural_you:Ustedes también son|Vosotros también sois}} como piedras vivas. Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} está edificando juntos como una casa donde vive {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Espíritu. Allí {{plural_you:sirven|servís}} como {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sacerdotes santos. Por medio de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}} {{plural_you:ofrecen|ofrecéis}} a Dios sacrificios espirituales que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} acepta con alegría.

sw.L: Mkimjia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, jiwe lililo hai, lililokataliwa kweli na wanadamu lakini mbele za Mungu lililochaguliwa [na] lenye thamani, \v 5 ninyi wenyewe pia mnajengwa kama mawe yaliyo hai [kuwa] nyumba ya kiroho, kwa ajili ya ukuhani mtakatifu, ili kutoa dhabihu za kiroho zinazokubalika kwa Mungu kupitia Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Mnamjia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, jiwe lililo hai ambalo wanadamu walilikataa kuwa halifai, lakini Mungu alilichagua na kulithamini. \v 5 Nanyi wenyewe, kama mawe yaliyo hai, mnajengwa kuwa nyumba kwa ajili ya Roho, ili mtumike kama ukuhani mtakatifu na kumtolea Mungu, kupitia Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, dhabihu za kiroho anazozipokea kwa furaha.
sw.R: Mnakuja kwa Bwana Yesu. Yeye ndiye jiwe lililo hai. Watu waliamua kwamba hafai, wakamkataa, lakini Mungu alimchagua, na kwa Mungu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni wa thamani kubwa. \v 5 Ninyi pia ni kama mawe yaliyo hai. Mungu anawajenga pamoja kuwa nyumba ambamo Roho {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} anakaa. Humo mnamtumikia kama makuhani {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} watakatifu. Kupitia Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} mnamtolea Mungu dhabihu za kiroho, naye anafurahi kuzipokea.

decisions.choice: to whom: the Lord of verse 3, Jesus
decisions.reason: ὃν picks up κύριος ("the Lord") at the end of verse 3. The stone is Christ (verses 6-8).

decisions.choice: coming: the readers keep coming to him
decisions.reason: προσερχόμενοι is a present participle: the readers come to Christ, and keep coming. In the Greek Old Testament the same verb is used of approaching God in worship, which fits the priesthood and sacrifices of verse 5.

decisions.choice: the rejected stone of Psalm 118:22 and the chosen, precious stone of Isaiah 28:16
decisions.reason: "Rejected" (ἀποδεδοκιμασμένον) and "chosen, precious" (ἐκλεκτὸν ἔντιμον) anticipate the quotations in verses 6-7. The verb means to test and throw out as unfit, as builders reject a stone. People judged Jesus worthless; God's verdict was the opposite.

decisions.choice: living stone; living stones
decisions.reason: A stone is not alive; the picture is deliberately strange. Christ is living because he is risen (1:3, 1:21), and those who come to him share his life and become living stones in the same building.

decisions.choice: you are being built: a statement of what God is doing
decisions.reason: οἰκοδομεῖσθε can be read as a statement or as a command; the forms are the same. The passive and the picture of a house God builds favor a statement: God is building them together.

decisions.choice: spiritual: belonging to and made by the Spirit
alternatives: spiritual as opposed to physical only
decisions.reason: πνευματικὸς in the New Testament usually means of the Spirit of God (1:2, 1:12). The house is a temple where the Spirit lives (compare 1 Corinthians 3:16), and its sacrifices are offered in the Spirit.

decisions.choice: a holy priesthood: the whole people serves God as priests
decisions.reason: ἱεράτευμα is a body of priests. All who come to Christ, not a special group among them, offer sacrifices to God. In 1 Peter these include praise (2:9) and a life of doing good (2:12; compare Hebrews 13:15-16; Romans 12:1). The same word comes again in verse 9.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπων means human beings, so the default is inclusive; "men" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: You come to the Lord Jesus.
decisions.reason: Readable names whom the readers come to (m1).

decisions.choice: a house for the Spirit (B); a house where his Spirit lives (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "spiritual" means here (m6); Literal keeps "spiritual".

decisions.choice: {{gender:People|Men}}
decisions.reason: Same setting as Literal and Balanced, at the start of a sentence.

decisions.choice: {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, so the default is inclusive; "los hombres" is the traditional form, as in the English setting.

decisions.choice: elegida (eligió)
decisions.reason: The same verb family as "elegidos", the letter's word for God's chosen people, so the chosen stone here and the chosen people of verse 9 are visibly linked.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives (yeye, wake)
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for God and Christ inside the verb ("mkimjia", "wakamkataa"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as elsewhere.

decisions.choice: wanadamu, no setting
decisions.reason: "Wanadamu" (human beings) and "watu" already include women and men, so Swahili has no gender span where the English has one, here and in verses 13 and 16.

source.text: διότι περιέχει ἐν γραφῇ· Ἰδοὺ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον ἀκρογωνιαῖον ἐκλεκτὸν ἔντιμον, καὶ ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ’ αὐτῷ οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ.

records.literal_gloss: Because it stands in Scripture: Behold, I lay in Zion a stone cornerstone chosen precious, and the [one] believing on him not not will be put to shame.

en.L: For it stands in Scripture: "Look, I am laying in Zion a stone, a chosen, precious cornerstone, and the one who believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} will by no means be put to shame."
en.B: For this is what Scripture says: "See, I am placing in Zion a stone, a cornerstone, chosen and precious, and no one who believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} will ever be put to shame."
en.R: For God says in Scripture: "Look! I am setting a stone in place in Zion. It is the cornerstone, the most important stone in the building. I chose it, and it is precious to me. Anyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} will never be let down or ashamed."

es.L: Porque está en [la] Escritura: «He aquí, pongo en Sion una piedra, piedra angular elegida, preciosa, y el que crea en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} de ningún modo será avergonzado».
es.B: Porque esto es lo que dice la Escritura: «Yo pongo en Sion una piedra, una piedra angular, elegida y preciosa; y el que crea en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} jamás será avergonzado».
es.R: Porque Dios dice en la Escritura: «Yo voy a poner en Sion una piedra. Es la piedra angular, la piedra más importante del edificio. Yo la elegí, y para mí es preciosa. El que crea en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nunca quedará defraudado ni avergonzado».

sw.L: Kwa sababu imo katika Maandiko: "Angalia, ninaweka katika Sayuni jiwe, jiwe kuu la pembeni lililochaguliwa, lenye thamani, na yule anayemwamini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hataaibishwa kamwe."
sw.B: Kwa maana Maandiko yanasema hivi: "Angalia, ninaweka katika Sayuni jiwe, jiwe kuu la pembeni, lililochaguliwa na lenye thamani; na yeyote anayemwamini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hataaibishwa kamwe."
sw.R: Kwa maana Mungu anasema katika Maandiko: "Angalia! Ninaweka jiwe mahali pake katika Sayuni. Ni jiwe kuu la pembeni, jiwe muhimu kuliko yote katika jengo. Nimelichagua, na ni la thamani kwangu. Yeyote anayemwamini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hatakatishwa tamaa wala hataaibishwa kamwe."

decisions.choice: Isaiah 28:16, quoted in the wording of the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 28:16 God promises a tested, precious cornerstone in Zion, in contrast with the leaders who trust in lies. Peter's wording is close to the Greek translation of Isaiah, which adds "in him" and has "will not be put to shame" where the Hebrew has "will not panic" or "will not be in a hurry". Paul quotes the same verse with Isaiah 8:14 in Romans 9:33, as Peter does in verses 6-8.

decisions.choice: it stands in Scripture
alternatives: it is contained in a writing
decisions.reason: περιέχει with ἐν γραφῇ is a way of introducing a quotation: "it says in Scripture". γραφῇ has no article, but it refers to the Scriptures of Israel.

decisions.choice: cornerstone: the main stone at the corner of the foundation
alternatives: capstone: the top stone of an arch or the last stone set at the top
decisions.reason: ἀκρογωνιαῖον is the stone at the corner that fixes the line of the whole building. In Isaiah 28:16 it is laid in the foundation, and the believer rests on it; that suits a foundation stone better than a stone at the top.

decisions.choice: in him: in Christ, the stone
alternatives: in it: in the stone, as a thing
decisions.reason: αὐτῷ refers to the stone, and Peter has already said the stone is Christ (verse 4). So the believer trusts in a person.

decisions.choice: will never be put to shame
decisions.reason: οὐ μὴ is the strongest way to deny something in Greek: it will by no means happen. To be put to shame is to have one's trust proved empty in the end, at God's judgment.

decisions.choice: Look (L, R); See (B)
decisions.reason: Modern English for the word that calls for attention; the style guide avoids "behold".

decisions.choice: For God says in Scripture
decisions.reason: The speaker in Isaiah 28:16 is God ("I am laying"); Readable says so.

decisions.choice: Yo pongo (B); Yo voy a poner (R)
decisions.reason: As in Romans 9:33, which quotes the same verse of Isaiah: "He aquí" (Literal) sounds archaic, and "miren" would add someone addressed, so Balanced and Readable give the emphasis with "yo".

decisions.choice: de ningún modo será avergonzado (L); jamás será avergonzado (B); nunca quedará ... avergonzado (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as Romans 9:33 ("será avergonzado", "quedará avergonzado"), so the reader sees that Peter and Paul quote one promise. Peter has the doubled negative, so each level adds "de ningún modo", "jamás" or "nunca".

decisions.choice: hataaibishwa kamwe
decisions.reason: The same verb as Romans 9:33 ("hataaibishwa"), which quotes the same verse of Isaiah; "kamwe" (never) gives the force of Peter's doubled negative.

source.text: ὑμῖν οὖν ἡ τιμὴ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν· ἀπιστοῦσιν δὲ λίθος ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας καὶ λίθος προσκόμματος καὶ πέτρα σκανδάλου· οἳ προσκόπτουσιν τῷ λόγῳ ἀπειθοῦντες· εἰς ὃ καὶ ἐτέθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: To you therefore the honor, the believing ones; to unbelieving ones however, [the] stone which rejected the building ones, this became into head of corner \v 8 and a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; who stumble at the word disobeying; to which also they were appointed.

en.L: To you, therefore, who believe [is] the honor; but to those who do not believe, "[The] stone which the builders rejected, this has become [the] head of [the] corner," \v 8 and "a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense." They stumble, disobeying the word; to this also they were appointed.
en.B: So the honor belongs to you who believe. But for those who do not believe, "The very stone the builders rejected has become the main cornerstone," \v 8 and "a stone they trip over, a rock that brings them down." They trip because they refuse to obey the word, and this is the end to which they were appointed.
en.R: So you who believe will receive honor. But for people who do not believe, Scripture says, "The stone that the builders rejected has become the most important stone of all." \v 8 It also says, "It is a stone that people trip over, a rock that makes them fall." They trip because they refuse to obey God's message. And this is what was appointed for them.

es.L: A {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pues, que {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}, [pertenece] el honor; pero para los que no creen, «[la] piedra que desecharon los edificadores, esta ha llegado a ser cabeza del ángulo», \v 8 y «una piedra de tropiezo y una roca de escándalo». Ellos tropiezan, desobedeciendo la palabra; para esto también fueron puestos.
es.B: Así que el honor es para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los que {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}. Pero para los que no creen, «la misma piedra que los constructores rechazaron se ha convertido en la principal piedra angular», \v 8 y «una piedra para tropezar, una roca que los hace caer». Tropiezan porque se niegan a obedecer la palabra, y ese es el fin para el cual fueron destinados.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los que {{plural_you:creen|creéis}}, {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}} honor. Pero para los que no creen, la Escritura dice: «La piedra que los constructores rechazaron ha llegado a ser la piedra más importante de todas». \v 8 Y también dice: «Es una piedra con la que la gente tropieza, una roca que los hace caer». Tropiezan porque se niegan a obedecer el mensaje de Dios. Y eso es lo que estaba destinado para ellos.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo heshima [ni] yenu mnaoamini; lakini kwa wasioamini, "Jiwe ambalo wajenzi walilikataa, hilo limekuwa kichwa cha pembeni," \v 8 na "jiwe la kukwaza na mwamba wa kikwazo." Wao wanajikwaa, wakiliasi neno; kwa hilo pia waliwekwa.
sw.B: Basi heshima ni yenu ninyi mnaoamini. Lakini kwa wale wasioamini, "Jiwe lilelile ambalo wajenzi walilikataa limekuwa jiwe kuu la pembeni," \v 8 na "jiwe la kujikwalia, mwamba unaowaangusha." Wanajikwaa kwa sababu wanakataa kulitii neno, na huo ndio mwisho waliowekewa.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo ninyi mnaoamini mtapata heshima. Lakini kwa watu wasioamini, Maandiko yanasema, "Jiwe ambalo wajenzi walilikataa limekuwa jiwe muhimu kuliko yote." \v 8 Tena yanasema, "Ni jiwe ambalo watu hujikwaa juu yake, mwamba unaowaangusha." Wanajikwaa kwa sababu wanakataa kutii ujumbe wa Mungu. Na hivyo ndivyo walivyowekewa.

decisions.choice: the honor is yours, you who believe
alternatives: he is precious to you who believe
decisions.reason: τιμὴ is the noun from the same root as ἔντιμον ("precious") in verse 6. It can mean honor or value. Read as "honor", it answers the last line of the quotation: those who believe will not be put to shame, so honor is theirs. Read as "preciousness", it means Christ is precious to them. The first fits the contrast with shame better, but the second is also possible.

decisions.choice: Psalm 118:22
decisions.reason: Psalm 118:22 (Greek Psalm 117:22): the stone the builders rejected has become the head of the corner. Jesus applied it to himself (Mark 12:10), and Peter used it before the council (Acts 4:11). The "builders" are those who should have recognized him.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 8:14
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 8:14 the Lord himself becomes a stone that makes people stumble and a rock that makes them fall, for those who will not trust him. Peter joins it to Psalm 118 and Isaiah 28, as Paul does in Romans 9:32-33. The stone that is the foundation for believers is the stone others trip over.

decisions.choice: a rock that makes people fall
decisions.reason: σκανδάλου was the trigger of a trap, and then anything that makes someone fall. Here it is parallel to "a stone of stumbling": the same rock brings people down.

decisions.choice: they stumble because they disobey the word
alternatives: they stumble at the word, being disobedient
decisions.reason: λόγῳ can go with "stumble" (they stumble at the word) or with ἀπειθοῦντες (disobeying the word). Either way the cause of stumbling is their refusal to obey the message about Christ (1:25; 3:1; 4:17). Unbelief in 1 Peter is disobedience, not only doubt.

decisions.choice: that is what they were appointed to: stumbling is the destined result of disobeying
alternatives: they were appointed to this end in God's plan, without saying how
decisions.reason: ἐτέθησαν is the same verb God uses in verse 6, "I am laying" (τίθημι). God has placed the stone, and he has also set the outcome: those who refuse it fall over it. The words say that their stumbling is not outside God's purpose. How far this reaches is debated: whether God appointed only the consequence of disobedience, or the persons themselves. The sentence itself names the stumbling of the disobedient as what was appointed.

decisions.choice: the main cornerstone (B); the most important stone of all (R)
decisions.reason: "The head of the corner" is an idiom for the cornerstone; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: Scripture says; It also says
decisions.reason: Readable marks the two quotations as Scripture, since the Greek runs them into Peter's sentence.

decisions.choice: God's message
decisions.reason: Readable says whose word is meant: the message about Christ (1:25).

decisions.choice: una piedra de tropiezo y una roca de escándalo (L); una piedra para tropezar, una roca que los hace caer (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same words as Romans 9:33, where Paul quotes the same line of Isaiah 8:14, so the two quotations read alike at each level.

decisions.choice: jiwe la kukwaza na mwamba wa kikwazo (L); jiwe la kujikwalia, mwamba unaowaangusha (B); mwamba unaowaangusha (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as Romans 9:33, where Paul quotes the same line of Isaiah 8:14, so the two quotations read alike at each level.

source.text: Ὑμεῖς δὲ γένος ἐκλεκτόν, βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα, ἔθνος ἅγιον, λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν, ὅπως τὰς ἀρετὰς ἐξαγγείλητε τοῦ ἐκ σκότους ὑμᾶς καλέσαντος εἰς τὸ θαυμαστὸν αὐτοῦ φῶς·

records.literal_gloss: You however [are] a race chosen, a royal priesthood, a nation holy, a people for possession, so that the excellencies you may proclaim of the [one] out of darkness you having called into the marvelous of him light;

en.L: But you [are] a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for [God's] possession, so that you may proclaim the excellencies of the one who called you out of darkness into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} marvelous light.
en.B: But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people God has claimed as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own, so that you may declare the great deeds of the one who called you out of the darkness into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} amazing light.
en.R: But you are the people God has chosen. You are priests who serve the King. You are a nation that belongs to God, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} very own people. God called you out of the darkness and brought you into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonderful light. Now you can tell others about the great things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes [son]|vosotros [sois]}} un linaje elegido, un sacerdocio real, una nación santa, un pueblo para posesión [de Dios], para que {{plural_you:proclamen|proclaméis}} las excelencias de aquel que {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó de [las] tinieblas a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} luz maravillosa.
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} un pueblo elegido, un sacerdocio real, una nación santa, un pueblo que Dios ha adquirido como {{deity_pronoun:suyo|Suyo}}, para que {{plural_you:proclamen|proclaméis}} las grandes obras de aquel que {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó de las tinieblas a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} luz maravillosa.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} el pueblo que Dios ha elegido. {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} sacerdotes que sirven al Rey. {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} una nación que pertenece a Dios, {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio pueblo. Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó a salir de la oscuridad y {{plural_you:los|os}} trajo a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} luz maravillosa. Ahora {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} contar a otros las grandes cosas que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha hecho.

sw.L: Lakini ninyi [ni] jamii teule, ukuhani wa kifalme, taifa takatifu, watu walio mali [ya Mungu], ili mtangaze ubora wa yule aliyewaita kutoka gizani kuingia katika nuru {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya kustaajabisha.
sw.B: Lakini ninyi ni jamii teule, ukuhani wa kifalme, taifa takatifu, watu ambao Mungu amewafanya kuwa mali {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mwenyewe, ili mtangaze matendo makuu ya yule aliyewaita kutoka gizani kuingia katika nuru {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya kustaajabisha.
sw.R: Lakini ninyi ni watu ambao Mungu amewachagua. Ninyi ni makuhani wanaomtumikia Mfalme. Ninyi ni taifa lililo mali ya Mungu, watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} hasa. Mungu aliwaita kutoka gizani, akawaleta katika nuru {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya ajabu. Sasa mnaweza kuwaambia wengine mambo makuu ambayo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} amefanya.

decisions.choice: Exodus 19:5-6 and Isaiah 43:20-21: the titles of Israel
decisions.reason: At Sinai God called Israel his own treasured possession, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation (Exodus 19:5-6). In Isaiah 43:20-21 he speaks of his chosen people, whom he formed for himself to declare his praise. Peter gives these titles to the churches he writes to, Jewish and Gentile believers together, because they belong to Christ.

decisions.choice: royal priesthood: priests who belong to the King and serve him
alternatives: a kingdom made up of priests
a house of kings and a body of priests
decisions.reason: βασίλειον usually means "royal", belonging to a king. The Greek of Exodus 19:6 has these same two words, translating the Hebrew "a kingdom of priests". Either way the people as a whole belong to God the King and serve him as priests (verse 5).

decisions.choice: a people for God's own possession
decisions.reason: περιποίησιν is something acquired and kept as one's own. The phrase recalls Malachi 3:17 and Isaiah 43:21: God has made this people his own.

decisions.choice: his excellencies: the great things God is and has done, which deserve praise
decisions.reason: ἀρετὰς usually means virtue or excellence. In the Greek of Isaiah 42:12 and 43:21 it stands for God's praise, the glory shown in his mighty deeds. ἐξαγγείλητε means to tell it out to others.

decisions.choice: called out of darkness into light: conversion
decisions.reason: God's call has moved them from ignorance of God (1:14, 1:18) into the light of knowing him (compare Colossians 1:13; Acts 26:18). The one who called is God (1:15; 5:10).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}
decisions.reason: Pronoun for God.

decisions.choice: a chosen people
decisions.reason: γένος is a people of one descent; "race" now suggests skin color, which is not the point. Literal keeps "race".

decisions.choice: the great deeds (B); the great things he has done (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what is to be proclaimed (m4). Literal keeps "excellencies".

decisions.choice: God called you ... Now you can tell others
alternatives: so that you may proclaim the excellencies of the one who called you
decisions.reason: Readable tells first what God did and then the purpose, in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: linaje
decisions.reason: Literal keeps a word of descent, but Spanish "raza" suggests skin color, as English "race" does; "linaje" says a people of one descent.

decisions.choice: jamii teule
decisions.reason: "Teule" (chosen) is the adjective of "wateule", the letter's word for God's chosen people, so the link to the chosen stone (verses 4, 6) and to 1:1 stays visible.

source.text: οἵ ποτε οὐ λαὸς νῦν δὲ λαὸς θεοῦ, οἱ οὐκ ἠλεημένοι νῦν δὲ ἐλεηθέντες.

records.literal_gloss: who once not a people but now a people of God, the [ones] not having been shown mercy but now having been shown mercy.

en.L: [You] who once [were] not a people but now [are] God's people, who had not been shown mercy but now have been shown mercy.
en.B: At one time you were no people at all; now you are God's people. You had been shown no mercy; now God has shown you mercy.
en.R: Before, you did not belong to any people. Now you belong to God's people. Before, you did not know God's mercy. But now God has been kind to you and shown you mercy.

es.L: [{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}], que antes no [{{plural_you:eran|erais}}] pueblo, pero ahora [{{plural_you:son|sois}}] pueblo de Dios; a quienes no se {{plural_you:les|os}} había mostrado misericordia, pero ahora se {{plural_you:les|os}} ha mostrado misericordia.
es.B: Hubo un tiempo en que no {{plural_you:eran|erais}} pueblo alguno; ahora {{plural_you:son|sois}} el pueblo de Dios. No se {{plural_you:les|os}} había mostrado misericordia; ahora Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} ha mostrado misericordia.
es.R: Antes no {{plural_you:pertenecían|pertenecíais}} a ningún pueblo. Ahora {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} al pueblo de Dios. Antes no {{plural_you:conocían|conocíais}} la misericordia de Dios. Pero ahora Dios ha sido bondadoso con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:les|os}} ha mostrado misericordia.

sw.L: [Ninyi] ambao zamani hamkuwa watu [wamoja], lakini sasa [ni] watu wa Mungu; ambao hamkuwa mmeonyeshwa rehema, lakini sasa mmeonyeshwa rehema.
sw.B: Wakati fulani hamkuwa watu wamoja; sasa ni watu wa Mungu. Hamkuwa mmeonyeshwa rehema; sasa Mungu amewaonyesha rehema.
sw.R: Zamani hamkuwa sehemu ya watu wowote. Sasa mmekuwa watu wa Mungu. Zamani hamkujua rehema ya Mungu. Lakini sasa Mungu amewafadhili na kuwaonyesha rehema.

decisions.choice: who: the "you" of verse 9
decisions.reason: οἵ continues the sentence about the readers. The SBLGNT ends verse 9 with a raised dot, so this description of who they are follows as its own sentence.

decisions.choice: Hosea 1:6-10 and 2:23
decisions.reason: Hosea gave his children the names "Not Pitied" and "Not My People" as a sign of God's judgment on Israel, and God promised to reverse them: "I will have pity on Not Pitied, and say to Not My People, You are my people" (Hosea 2:23). Paul applies the same promise to Gentiles in Romans 9:25-26. Here it describes believers who once had no part in God's people and now belong to it.

decisions.choice: had not received mercy, now have received mercy
decisions.reason: ἠλεημένοι (perfect) describes their lasting state before: they were people without mercy. ἐλεηθέντες (aorist) points to the moment God showed them mercy, in their new birth (1:3).

decisions.choice: [You] who
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the subject so that the sentence can be read on its own.

decisions.choice: pueblo; misericordia
decisions.reason: The Hosea promise is the one Paul quotes in Romans 9:25-26, where Spanish has "pueblo" ("mi pueblo"); the same word is used here, with "misericordia", the settled word for mercy.

decisions.choice: hamkuwa watu [wamoja]
decisions.reason: "Hamkuwa watu" alone could be read as "you were not human beings". "Watu wamoja" (one people) makes clear that a people is meant, and "watu wa Mungu" matches "watu wangu" in Romans 9:25-26, the same Hosea promise.

source.text: Ἀγαπητοί, παρακαλῶ ὡς παροίκους καὶ παρεπιδήμους ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν σαρκικῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν, αἵτινες στρατεύονται κατὰ τῆς ψυχῆς·

records.literal_gloss: Beloved, I urge as foreigners and temporary residents to abstain from the fleshly desires, which wage war against the soul;

en.L: Beloved, I urge [you] as foreigners and temporary residents to abstain from the fleshly desires, which wage war against the soul.
en.B: Dear friends, you live here as outsiders and temporary residents. So I urge you to keep away from the cravings of the flesh, for they fight against your soul.
en.R: Dear friends, this world is not your real home. You are like foreigners living here for a while. So I urge you: do not give in to the wrong desires of your sinful nature. They are at war with your very life.

es.L: Amados, {{plural_you:les|os}} ruego, como a forasteros y extranjeros, que {{plural_you:se abstengan|os abstengáis}} de los deseos carnales, que hacen guerra contra el alma.
es.B: Queridos amigos, {{plural_you:ustedes viven|vosotros vivís}} aquí como forasteros y extranjeros. Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} ruego que {{plural_you:se aparten|os apartéis}} de los deseos de la carne, porque luchan contra {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} alma.
es.R: Queridos amigos, este mundo no es {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} verdadero hogar. {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} como extranjeros que viven aquí por un tiempo. Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} ruego: no {{plural_you:cedan|cedáis}} a los malos deseos de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} naturaleza pecadora. Esos deseos están en guerra contra {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida misma.

sw.L: Wapendwa, nawasihi kama wakaaji wa kigeni na wageni mjiepushe na tamaa za kimwili, ambazo zinapigana vita dhidi ya nafsi.
sw.B: Wapendwa, mnaishi hapa kama wakaaji wa kigeni na wageni. Kwa hiyo nawasihi mjiepushe na tamaa za mwili, kwa maana zinapigana dhidi ya nafsi zenu.
sw.R: Wapendwa, dunia hii si nyumbani kwenu halisi. Ninyi ni kama wageni wanaoishi hapa kwa muda tu. Kwa hiyo nawasihi: msikubali kutawaliwa na tamaa mbaya za asili yenu ya dhambi. Tamaa hizo zinapigana vita dhidi ya uhai wenu wenyewe.

decisions.choice: foreigners and temporary residents: people who live where they do not belong
decisions.reason: παροίκους was a resident foreigner, living in a place without citizen rights; παρεπιδήμους was someone staying for a while, away from home (1:1, 1:17). Abraham called himself both (Genesis 23:4, in the Greek Old Testament). Peter means that believers do not belong to the ways of the world around them; their home is with God. Some of them may also have been foreigners in the legal sense.

decisions.choice: desires of the flesh: cravings of human nature turned away from God
decisions.reason: σαρκικῶν describes what belongs to the flesh, human life apart from God. The desires include more than bodily appetites; compare 4:2-3 and Galatians 5:19-21.

decisions.choice: the soul: the person's true life before God
alternatives: the immaterial part as opposed to the body
decisions.reason: ψυχῆς in 1 Peter is the whole self, the life God saves (1:9, 1:22; 2:25). These desires make war on that life.

decisions.choice: Dear friends
decisions.reason: Ἀγαπητοί means "loved ones"; "dear friends" says the same in ordinary speech. Literal keeps "Beloved".

decisions.choice: you live here as outsiders and temporary residents. So I urge you (B); this world is not your real home (R)
alternatives: I urge you as foreigners and exiles
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state first what the readers are, then the appeal that follows from it. Readable says plainly what the picture means (m1).

decisions.choice: forasteros y extranjeros
decisions.reason: "Extranjeros" is the letter's word for the readers as exiles (1:1) and renders the second word; "forasteros" renders the first, the resident outsider. "Peregrinos" would suggest pilgrims on a journey to a shrine.

decisions.choice: wakaaji wa kigeni na wageni
decisions.reason: "Wageni" is the letter's word for the readers as exiles (1:1) and renders the second word; "wakaaji wa kigeni" (foreign residents) renders the first, someone living in a place where he is not a citizen.

source.text: τὴν ἀναστροφὴν ὑμῶν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἔχοντες καλήν, ἵνα, ἐν ᾧ καταλαλοῦσιν ὑμῶν ὡς κακοποιῶν, ἐκ τῶν καλῶν ἔργων ἐποπτεύοντες δοξάσωσι τὸν θεὸν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ἐπισκοπῆς.

records.literal_gloss: the conduct of you among the Gentiles keeping good, so that, in which they speak against you as evildoers, from the good works observing they may glorify the God in day of visitation.

en.L: keeping your conduct among the Gentiles good, so that, in the very thing in which they speak against you as evildoers, by observing [your] good works they may glorify God in [the] day of visitation.
en.B: Let your way of life among those who do not know God be honorable. Then, though they speak against you as wrongdoers, they will see your good works for themselves and glorify God on the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} visits.
en.R: Live good lives among the people around you who do not know God. They may say you are doing wrong. But they will see the good things you do, and they will give glory to God on the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes.

es.L: teniendo {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} conducta buena entre los gentiles, para que, en lo mismo en que hablan contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} como malhechores, al observar [{{plural_you:sus|vuestras}}] buenas obras glorifiquen a Dios en [el] día de [la] visitación.
es.B: Que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} manera de vivir entre los que no conocen a Dios sea honorable. Así, aunque hablen contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} como si {{plural_you:fueran|fuerais}} malhechores, verán por sí mismos {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} buenas obras y glorificarán a Dios el día en que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los visite.
es.R: {{plural_you:Vivan|Vivid}} una vida buena entre la gente que no conoce a Dios. Puede que digan que {{plural_you:ustedes hacen|vosotros hacéis}} el mal. Pero verán el bien que {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}, y darán gloria a Dios el día en que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} venga.

sw.L: mkiudumisha mwenendo wenu kati ya watu wa mataifa kuwa mzuri, ili, katika jambo lile wanalowasingizia kuwa watenda maovu, wakiyaona matendo [yenu] mema, wamtukuze Mungu katika siku ya kujiliwa.
sw.B: Mwenendo wenu kati ya watu wasiomjua Mungu uwe wa heshima. Hapo, ingawa wanawasema kuwa watenda mabaya, watayaona matendo yenu mema wao wenyewe na kumtukuza Mungu siku atakapowajia.
sw.R: Ishini maisha mema kati ya watu wanaowazunguka wasiomjua Mungu. Huenda wakasema kwamba mnatenda mabaya. Lakini wataona mambo mema mnayoyafanya, nao watampa Mungu utukufu siku atakapokuja.

decisions.choice: keeping your conduct good: goes with the appeal of verse 11
decisions.reason: ἔχοντες is a participle that continues verse 11: abstaining from evil desires goes with keeping an honorable way of life. καλήν means good in the sense of fine, admirable, what others can see is good.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: people who do not know God
decisions.reason: ἔθνεσιν is Israel's word for the other nations. Most of Peter's readers were Gentiles by birth (1:14, 1:18; 4:3), so here the word means the unbelieving world around them, now seen from inside God's people.

decisions.choice: they speak against you as evildoers
decisions.reason: Believers were suspected of bad conduct because they kept away from temple feasts and festivals, worshiped no other god, and met privately (4:3-4). The accusation was common; the letter answers it by good conduct, not by argument.

decisions.choice: the day of visitation: the day God comes
alternatives: the day God comes in judgment only
the day God visits them with salvation, when they believe
decisions.reason: ἐπισκοπῆς is God's coming to look into things and act, whether to save or to judge (Isaiah 10:3; Luke 19:44). Here it probably means the final day, when those who once slandered believers will give glory to God. Whether they will do so as people who have come to believe, or as people forced to admit the truth, is not stated; the first fits Matthew 5:16 and 3:1 of this letter.

decisions.choice: those who do not know God (B); the people around you who do not know God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "Gentiles" means here (m2), since the readers were themselves mostly Gentiles. Literal keeps "Gentiles".

decisions.choice: on the day he visits (B); on the day he comes (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the one who visits. Literal keeps the phrase.

decisions.choice: Let your way of life ... be honorable (B); Live good lives (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable begin a new sentence, so the participle becomes a command, as it is in sense (m1). Literal keeps the participle.

decisions.choice: los que no conocen a Dios (B); la gente que no conoce a Dios (R)
decisions.reason: The usual Readable wording for this word, "los que no son judíos", does not fit here: the readers were mostly Gentiles themselves, and the meaning decision reads the word as the unbelieving world around them.

decisions.choice: watu wasiomjua Mungu
decisions.reason: The usual Readable wording for this word, "watu wasio Wayahudi", does not fit here: the readers were mostly Gentiles themselves, and the meaning decision reads the word as the unbelieving world around them.

source.text: Ὑποτάγητε πάσῃ ἀνθρωπίνῃ κτίσει διὰ τὸν κύριον· εἴτε βασιλεῖ ὡς ὑπερέχοντι, εἴτε ἡγεμόσιν ὡς δι’ αὐτοῦ πεμπομένοις εἰς ἐκδίκησιν κακοποιῶν ἔπαινον δὲ ἀγαθοποιῶν ὅτι οὕτως ἐστὶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀγαθοποιοῦντας φιμοῦν τὴν τῶν ἀφρόνων ἀνθρώπων ἀγνωσίαν·

records.literal_gloss: Be subject to every human institution because of the Lord; whether to king as being supreme, \v 14 or to governors as through him being sent for punishment of evildoers and praise of those doing good; \v 15 because thus is the will of the God, doing good to muzzle the of the foolish men ignorance;

en.L: Be subject to every human institution for the sake of the Lord, whether to [the] king as being supreme, \v 14 or to governors as sent by him for punishment of evildoers and praise of those who do good; \v 15 because so is the will of God, [that] by doing good [you] silence the ignorance of foolish {{gender:people|men}}.
en.B: For the Lord's sake, place yourselves under every authority that people have set up: the emperor, who holds the highest rank, \v 14 and the governors he sends out to punish wrongdoing and to reward good conduct with praise. \v 15 For this is God's will: that by doing good you muzzle the ignorance of foolish {{gender:people|men}}.
en.R: Because you belong to the Lord, respect every human authority and accept its rule. Respect the emperor, because he is the highest ruler. \v 14 Respect the governors too. The emperor sends them to punish those who do wrong and to praise those who do right. \v 15 God wants you to do good. When you do, foolish {{gender:people|men}} who talk about you without knowing what they are saying will have nothing more to say.

es.L: {{plural_you:Sométanse|Someteos}} a toda institución humana por causa del Señor; sea al rey, como el que está por encima, \v 14 sea a [los] gobernadores, como enviados por él para castigar a los malhechores y alabar a los que hacen el bien; \v 15 porque así es la voluntad de Dios: [que] haciendo el bien {{plural_you:silencien|silenciéis}} la ignorancia de {{gender:las personas insensatas|los hombres insensatos}}.
es.B: Por amor al Señor, {{plural_you:pónganse|poneos}} bajo toda autoridad que los seres humanos han establecido: el emperador, que ocupa el rango más alto, \v 14 y los gobernadores que él envía para castigar el mal y premiar con elogios la buena conducta. \v 15 Porque esta es la voluntad de Dios: que, haciendo el bien, {{plural_you:silencien|silenciéis}} la ignorancia de {{gender:las personas insensatas|los hombres insensatos}}.
es.R: Porque {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} al Señor, {{plural_you:respeten|respetad}} a toda autoridad humana y {{plural_you:acepten|aceptad}} su gobierno. {{plural_you:Respeten|Respetad}} al emperador, porque es el gobernante más alto. \v 14 {{plural_you:Respeten|Respetad}} también a los gobernadores. El emperador los envía para castigar a los que hacen el mal y para alabar a los que hacen el bien. \v 15 Dios quiere que {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} el bien. Cuando lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}, {{gender:las personas insensatas|los hombres insensatos}} que hablan de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} sin saber lo que dicen ya no tendrán nada que decir.

sw.L: Nyenyekeeni kila mamlaka ya kibinadamu kwa ajili ya Bwana; ikiwa ni mfalme, kama aliye mkuu kuliko wote, \v 14 au watawala, kama waliotumwa naye kwa ajili ya kuwaadhibu watenda maovu na kuwasifu watenda mema; \v 15 kwa sababu ndivyo yalivyo mapenzi ya Mungu, [kwamba] kwa kutenda mema mnyamazishe ujinga wa watu wapumbavu.
sw.B: Kwa ajili ya Bwana, nyenyekeeni kila mamlaka iliyowekwa na wanadamu: Kaisari, aliye na cheo cha juu kuliko wote, \v 14 na watawala anaowatuma kuadhibu maovu na kusifu mwenendo mwema. \v 15 Kwa maana haya ndiyo mapenzi ya Mungu: kwamba kwa kutenda mema mnyamazishe ujinga wa watu wapumbavu.
sw.R: Kwa kuwa ninyi ni wa Bwana, heshimuni kila mamlaka ya kibinadamu na mkubali utawala wake. Mheshimuni Kaisari, kwa sababu yeye ndiye mtawala mkuu kuliko wote. \v 14 Waheshimuni pia watawala. Kaisari huwatuma ili wawaadhibu wale wanaotenda mabaya na kuwasifu wale wanaotenda mema. \v 15 Mungu anataka mtende mema. Mnapofanya hivyo, watu wapumbavu wanaowasema bila kujua wanachosema watakosa la kusema.

decisions.choice: be subject: accept your place under their authority
decisions.reason: Ὑποτάγητε means to place oneself under someone in an order. It asks for respect and cooperation, not for doing whatever is commanded: the same letter tells believers to fear God (verse 17) and not to fear what others fear (3:14), and the apostles refused an order to stop preaching (Acts 5:29).

decisions.choice: every human institution: every authority set up among people
alternatives: every human creature: every human being
decisions.reason: κτίσει normally means creation or a creature, so the phrase could mean "every human being" (compare "honor everyone" in verse 17). But the examples that follow are the emperor and governors, and the word was also used of something established or founded. So it is read here as human authorities.

decisions.choice: for the Lord's sake: because of Christ
decisions.reason: κύριον is Christ, as in 2:3 and 3:15. Believers accept human authority because of their loyalty to him and so that his name is not slandered (verse 12).

decisions.choice: the king: the Roman emperor
decisions.reason: βασιλεῖ was the ordinary Greek title for the Roman emperor in the eastern provinces. He ruled over all the provinces Peter writes to (1:1); governors were his appointed officials there.

decisions.choice: sent by him: sent by the emperor
decisions.reason: αὐτοῦ most naturally refers to the king just named. Governors in the provinces held power from the emperor. That God stands behind all such authority is said elsewhere (Romans 13:1), not here.

decisions.choice: this is God's will: that by doing good you silence ignorant people
alternatives: this is God's will, as just said; doing good, you silence them
decisions.reason: οὕτως points forward to the participle and infinitive that follow. God wants his people to answer slander by doing good.

decisions.choice: to silence: to muzzle
decisions.reason: φιμοῦν means to muzzle an animal, and then to silence someone. Good conduct leaves the accusers with nothing to say.

decisions.choice: the emperor
decisions.reason: In English "the king" suggests a monarch of one nation; the person meant was the Roman emperor (m4). Literal keeps "king".

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπων means human beings; "men" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: Because you belong to the Lord
alternatives: for the sake of the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable says why "for the Lord's sake" matters to the readers (m3).

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Sométanse|Someteos}}
decisions.reason: "Someterse" is used for this verb here, for household servants in verse 18 and for wives in 3:1, so Literal shows that one verb runs through the household instructions.

decisions.choice: nyenyekeeni
decisions.reason: "Kunyenyekea" (to submit, place oneself under) is used for this verb here, for household servants in verse 18 and for wives in 3:1, as in Ephesians 5. "Kutii" (obey) would say more than the meaning decision allows.

decisions.choice: Kaisari
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Roman emperor (meaning decision on the king). "Kaisari" is the title Swahili readers know from the Gospels for the emperor in Rome; Literal keeps "mfalme".

source.text: ὡς ἐλεύθεροι, καὶ μὴ ὡς ἐπικάλυμμα ἔχοντες τῆς κακίας τὴν ἐλευθερίαν, ἀλλ’ ὡς θεοῦ δοῦλοι.

records.literal_gloss: as free, and not as a covering having of the evil the freedom, but as of God slaves.

en.L: [Live] as free {{gender:people|men}}, and not as [those] having freedom as a covering for evil, but as slaves of God.
en.B: Act as free {{gender:people|men}}. Your freedom is not a mask for wickedness; you are slaves who belong to God.
en.R: You are free. But do not use your freedom as an excuse to do wrong. Live as God's slaves, people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: [{{plural_you:Vivan|Vivid}}] como {{gender:personas libres|hombres libres}}, y no como [quienes] tienen la libertad como cubierta de la maldad, sino como esclavos de Dios.
es.B: {{plural_you:Actúen|Actuad}} como {{gender:personas libres|hombres libres}}. {{plural_you:Su|Vuestra}} libertad no es una máscara para la maldad; {{plural_you:son|sois}} esclavos que pertenecen a Dios.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} libres. Pero no {{plural_you:usen|uséis}} {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} libertad como excusa para hacer el mal. {{plural_you:Vivan|Vivid}} como esclavos de Dios, personas que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pertenecen.

sw.L: [Ishini] kama watu huru, wala si kama [wale] walio na uhuru kama kifuniko cha uovu, bali kama watumwa wa Mungu.
sw.B: Enendeni kama watu huru. Uhuru wenu si kinyago cha kuficha uovu; ninyi ni watumwa walio mali ya Mungu.
sw.R: Ninyi ni watu huru. Lakini msitumie uhuru wenu kama sababu ya kutenda mabaya. Ishini kama watumwa wa Mungu, watu walio mali {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

decisions.choice: as free people: describes how they are to be subject (verse 13)
decisions.reason: ἐλεύθεροι has no verb of its own. The SBLGNT ends the sentence at verse 15 with a raised dot and at verse 16 with a full stop, so verse 16 continues "be subject": believers submit not as people forced to, but as free people.

decisions.choice: free, yet slaves of God
decisions.reason: Their freedom is real: they have been ransomed from their old way of life (1:18). But it is not freedom to do evil; it is the freedom of people who now belong wholly to God. ἐπικάλυμμα is a covering or veil: freedom must not be used to hide wrongdoing.

decisions.choice: slaves of God: people who belong entirely to God
alternatives: servants of God (in a looser sense)
decisions.reason: δοῦλοι is a slave, someone owned by another. Israel's prophets and leaders were called slaves of God, and believers now are (Romans 6:22; Philippians 1:1). The word stresses belonging and obedience; it points ahead to the household slaves addressed in verse 18.

decisions.choice: [Live] as free
decisions.reason: Literal supplies a verb so the sentence can be read on its own.

decisions.choice: free {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means free persons, men and women; "free men" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" for this word at every level (style guide), so that the contrast with "free" stays sharp (m3).

decisions.choice: {{gender:personas libres|hombres libres}}
decisions.reason: The word means free persons, men and women; "hombres libres" is the traditional form, as in the English setting.

decisions.choice: esclavos
decisions.reason: "Esclavo" for this word at every level, as in Paul's letters, so that the contrast with "libres" stays sharp. "Siervos" would soften it.

decisions.choice: watumwa
decisions.reason: "Mtumwa" for this word at every level, as in Paul's letters, so that the contrast with "huru" stays sharp. "Watumishi" (servants) would soften it.

source.text: πάντας τιμήσατε, τὴν ἀδελφότητα ἀγαπᾶτε, τὸν θεὸν φοβεῖσθε, τὸν βασιλέα τιμᾶτε.

records.literal_gloss: All honor, the brotherhood love, the God fear, the king honor.

en.L: Honor all, love the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brotherhood}}, fear God, honor the king.
en.B: Give honor to every person. Love your fellow believers. Fear God. Give honor to the emperor.
en.R: Show respect to everyone. Love God's family, your fellow believers. Have reverence for God. Show respect to the emperor.

es.L: {{plural_you:Honren|Honrad}} a todos, {{plural_you:amen|amad}} a la hermandad, {{plural_you:teman|temed}} a Dios, {{plural_you:honren|honrad}} al rey.
es.B: {{plural_you:Den|Dad}} honor a toda persona. {{plural_you:Amen|Amad}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hermanos en la fe. {{plural_you:Teman|Temed}} a Dios. {{plural_you:Den|Dad}} honor al emperador.
es.R: {{plural_you:Muestren|Mostrad}} respeto a todos. {{plural_you:Amen|Amad}} a la familia de Dios, a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hermanos en la fe. {{plural_you:Reverencien|Reverenciad}} a Dios. {{plural_you:Muestren|Mostrad}} respeto al emperador.

sw.L: Waheshimuni wote, upendeni udugu, mcheni Mungu, mheshimuni mfalme.
sw.B: Mpeni kila mtu heshima. Wapendeni ndugu zenu katika imani. Mcheni Mungu. Mpeni Kaisari heshima.
sw.R: Waheshimuni watu wote. Ipendeni familia ya Mungu, yaani ndugu zenu waumini. Mcheni Mungu. Mheshimuni Kaisari.

decisions.choice: the brotherhood: the whole community of believers
decisions.reason: ἀδελφότητα is the family of brothers and sisters in Christ, everywhere in the world (5:9). Love for them is the love of 1:22.

decisions.choice: honor all, including the emperor; fear God alone
decisions.reason: The emperor receives the same honor (τιμᾶτε) as everyone (τιμήσατε); only God is to be feared. The saying recalls Proverbs 24:21 (fear God and the king) but changes it: the king is honored, not feared.

decisions.choice: honor everyone: the heading over the three commands that follow
decisions.reason: The first verb (τιμήσατε) is aorist and the other three are present. Some read the first as a general command that the other three spell out; others read four equal commands. The meaning is little affected.

decisions.choice: the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brotherhood}}
decisions.reason: Inclusive default, as the word means the community of brothers and sisters; "the brotherhood" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: your fellow believers (B); God's family, your fellow believers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the brotherhood is (m1).

decisions.choice: the emperor
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: Show respect (R); Have reverence for God (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for honor and for the fear of God, which is reverence, not terror.

decisions.choice: la hermandad (L); hermanos (B, R), no setting
decisions.reason: Spanish "hermandad" and "hermanos" already take in brothers and sisters, so there is no gender span where the English has one.

decisions.choice: udugu (L); ndugu (B, R), no setting
decisions.reason: "Udugu" and "ndugu" already take in brothers and sisters, so Swahili has no gender span where the English has one.

source.text: Οἱ οἰκέται ὑποτασσόμενοι ἐν παντὶ φόβῳ τοῖς δεσπόταις, οὐ μόνον τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς καὶ ἐπιεικέσιν ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς σκολιοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: The household slaves, being subject in all fear to the masters, not only to the good and gentle but also to the crooked.

en.L: Household slaves, [be] subject with all fear to [your] masters, not only to the good and gentle but also to the crooked.
en.B: Household slaves, place yourselves under your masters with deep reverence, not just those who are kind and gentle but also those who are crooked and harsh.
en.R: You who are slaves in a household, respect your masters and accept their authority. Do this out of reverence for God. Do it whether your masters are kind and gentle or cruel and unfair.

es.L: Criados, [{{plural_you:estén|estad}}] sometidos con todo temor a [{{plural_you:sus|vuestros}}] amos, no solo a los buenos y amables, sino también a los torcidos.
es.B: Criados, {{plural_you:sométanse|someteos}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} amos con profunda reverencia, no solo a los que son buenos y comprensivos, sino también a los que son injustos y duros.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los que {{plural_you:sirven|servís}} como criados en una casa, {{plural_you:respeten|respetad}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} amos y {{plural_you:acepten|aceptad}} su autoridad. {{plural_you:Háganlo|Hacedlo}} por reverencia a Dios. {{plural_you:Háganlo|Hacedlo}} tanto si {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} amos son buenos y amables como si son crueles e injustos.

sw.L: Watumishi wa nyumbani, [muwe] mkiwanyenyekea mabwana [wenu] kwa hofu yote, si kwa walio wema na wenye upole peke yao, bali pia kwa walio wapotovu.
sw.B: Watumishi wa nyumbani, wanyenyekeeni mabwana wenu kwa heshima kuu, wala si wale wema na wenye upole tu, bali hata wale wakorofi na wakali.
sw.R: Ninyi mlio watumishi wa nyumbani, waheshimuni mabwana wenu na mkubali mamlaka yao. Fanyeni hivyo kwa sababu mnamcha Mungu. Fanyeni hivyo iwe mabwana wenu ni wema na wapole, au ni wakatili na madhalimu.

decisions.choice: household slaves in the Roman world; what the letter does and does not address
decisions.reason: Many households included slaves, who were their owners' legal property and could be beaten (verse 20). Some held responsible posts; others did hard labor. Many were later freed. Peter speaks to believing slaves, many of whom had masters who did not share their faith and could be cruel. Unlike Colossians 3:22-4:1 and Ephesians 6:5-9, he gives no word to masters. The letter does not discuss whether slavery should exist. It tells slaves how to live under unjust treatment as people who belong to God (verse 16) and follow Christ's example (verses 21-25). It does not say that their suffering is deserved or that God approves of cruelty.

decisions.choice: household slaves
decisions.reason: οἰκέται is a different word from δοῦλος. It means a member of a household's staff, and in practice nearly always a slave who worked in the house. The word is chosen for the household setting, not to describe a freer status: these people could be struck by their owners (verse 20). The owners are δεσπόταις, a word for absolute owners and masters.

decisions.choice: be subject: a participle used as a command
decisions.reason: ὑποτασσόμενοι is a participle with no main verb; as often in household instructions, it gives a command. It applies to slaves the same verb as verse 13 (be subject).

decisions.choice: with all fear: reverence for God
decisions.reason: In 1 Peter the one to be feared is God (1:17; 2:17), and believers are told not to fear people (3:6, 3:14). So φόβῳ here most likely means reverence for God, which shapes how slaves act toward their masters.

decisions.choice: the crooked: harsh, unjust masters
decisions.reason: σκολιοῖς means bent or crooked, and then perverse or unfair. The contrast is with masters who are good and ἐπιεικέσιν (gentle, reasonable).

decisions.choice: household slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" is the style guide's word for the person's position, and "household" keeps what this word adds (m2). "Servants" would suggest free people working for pay.

decisions.choice: out of reverence for God
decisions.reason: Readable names whom the fear is for (m4).

decisions.choice: criados
decisions.reason: As in Romans 14:4, "criado" is kept for this word, a member of a household's staff, so that it stays distinct from "esclavo" (verse 16) and "servidor". The meaning decision says these people were in practice slaves who could be beaten (verse 20), which the English makes explicit with "household slaves"; a reviewer may prefer "esclavos domésticos".

decisions.choice: watumishi wa nyumbani
decisions.reason: As in Romans 14:4, "mtumishi wa nyumbani" is kept for this word, a member of a household's staff, so that it stays distinct from "mtumwa" (verse 16) and "mtumishi". The meaning decision says these people were in practice slaves who could be beaten (verse 20), which the English makes explicit with "household slaves"; a reviewer may prefer "watumwa wa nyumbani".

source.text: τοῦτο γὰρ χάρις εἰ διὰ συνείδησιν θεοῦ ὑποφέρει τις λύπας πάσχων ἀδίκως·

records.literal_gloss: This for [is] grace, if because of consciousness of God endures someone griefs, suffering unjustly;

en.L: For this [is] grace, if, because of awareness of God, someone endures griefs, suffering unjustly.
en.B: For this finds favor: when someone, mindful of God, bears up under pain while suffering unjustly.
en.R: God is pleased when someone suffers unfairly and bears the pain because {{gender:they keep|he keeps}} God in mind.

es.L: Porque esto [es] gracia, si, a causa de [la] conciencia de Dios, alguien soporta penas, sufriendo injustamente.
es.B: Porque esto halla favor: que alguien, consciente de Dios, soporte el dolor cuando sufre injustamente.
es.R: Dios se agrada cuando alguien sufre injustamente y soporta el dolor porque tiene presente a Dios.

sw.L: Kwa maana hii [ni] neema, ikiwa, kwa sababu ya kumtambua Mungu, mtu anastahimili huzuni, akiteswa kwa udhalimu.
sw.B: Kwa maana hili linapata kibali: mtu anapovumilia maumivu akiteswa kwa udhalimu, kwa kuwa anamkumbuka Mungu.
sw.R: Mungu anapendezwa mtu anapoteswa bila kosa na kuvumilia maumivu kwa sababu anamweka Mungu akilini.

decisions.choice: grace here: what finds favor with God
decisions.reason: χάρις here does not mean God's gift of salvation but something that wins favor, as verse 20 shows: "this is χάρις with God" (compare Luke 6:32-34, where the word means credit or thanks). Enduring unjust suffering for God's sake is what God looks on with favor. The word is still the letter's word for grace (1:2, 5:12), and that link may be intended.

decisions.choice: awareness of God: because one is mindful of God
decisions.reason: συνείδησιν with θεοῦ is consciousness of God: the slave bears unjust treatment because he or she knows God sees and keeps faith with God.

decisions.choice: someone: any believer, though slaves are addressed
decisions.reason: τις makes a general statement. It applies first to the slaves of verse 18, but the same holds for any believer who suffers unjustly (3:14, 3:17; 4:14-16).

decisions.choice: this finds favor (B); God is pleased (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense (m1). Literal keeps the word "grace" so that the reader sees it.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they keep|he keeps}}
decisions.reason: Singular "they" for someone; "he" is the traditional form.

source.text: ποῖον γὰρ κλέος εἰ ἁμαρτάνοντες καὶ κολαφιζόμενοι ὑπομενεῖτε;

records.literal_gloss: What kind for credit [is it] if sinning and being struck you will endure?

en.L: For what credit [is it] if, when you sin and are struck, you endure [it]?
en.B: For what is praiseworthy about putting up with blows when you have done wrong?
en.R: If you are beaten because you did wrong, and you put up with it, you deserve no praise for that.

es.L: Porque ¿qué mérito [hay] si, cuando {{plural_you:pecan|pecáis}} y {{plural_you:son|sois}} abofeteados, lo {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}}?
es.B: Porque ¿qué tiene de admirable soportar golpes cuando {{plural_you:han|habéis}} hecho el mal?
es.R: Si {{plural_you:los|os}} golpean porque {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} algo malo, y lo {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}}, no {{plural_you:merecen|merecéis}} ningún elogio por ello.

sw.L: Kwa maana ni sifa gani ikiwa, mkitenda dhambi na kupigwa ngumi, mtastahimili?
sw.B: Kwa maana kuna fahari gani kuvumilia mapigo mkiwa mmetenda mabaya?
sw.R: Mkipigwa kwa sababu mlitenda mabaya, nanyi mkavumilia, hamstahili kusifiwa kwa hilo.

decisions.choice: being struck: beaten with fists
decisions.reason: κολαφιζόμενοι means to hit with the fist. It is what was done to Jesus (Mark 14:65), and what slaves could expect from their owners.

decisions.choice: credit: praise or fame
decisions.reason: κλέος is fame or praise. A slave who endures a deserved beating earns nothing for it, before people or before God.

decisions.choice: you deserve no praise for that
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

source.text: ἀλλ’ εἰ ἀγαθοποιοῦντες καὶ πάσχοντες ὑπομενεῖτε, τοῦτο χάρις παρὰ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: But if doing good and suffering you will endure, this [is] grace with God.

en.L: But if, when you do good and suffer, you endure [it], this [is] grace with God.
en.B: But if you do good and suffer for it and you endure, this finds favor with God.
en.R: But suppose you do what is right and you suffer for it. If you bear it patiently, God is pleased with you.

es.L: Pero si, cuando {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} el bien y {{plural_you:sufren|sufrís}}, lo {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}}, esto [es] gracia ante Dios.
es.B: Pero si {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} el bien y {{plural_you:sufren|sufrís}} por ello, y lo {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}}, esto halla favor ante Dios.
es.R: Pero supongamos que {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} lo correcto y {{plural_you:sufren|sufrís}} por ello. Si lo {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}} con paciencia, Dios se agrada de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa, mkitenda mema na kuteswa, mtastahimili, hii [ni] neema mbele za Mungu.
sw.B: Lakini mkitenda mema na kuteswa kwa sababu hiyo, nanyi mkavumilia, hilo linapata kibali mbele za Mungu.
sw.R: Lakini tuseme mnatenda yaliyo mema, nanyi mnateswa kwa sababu hiyo. Mkivumilia kwa subira, Mungu anapendezwa nanyi.

decisions.choice: grace with God: what God approves
alternatives: a gift of grace from God
decisions.reason: As in verse 19, χάρις here is favor: patient endurance of suffering for doing good is what God looks on with approval.

decisions.choice: doing good and suffering, you endure: suffering because of the good one does
decisions.reason: ἀγαθοποιοῦντες and πάσχοντες stand side by side: those who do right and suffer for it (3:14, 3:17). ὑπομενεῖτε is to bear up, to stand firm under it.

decisions.choice: this finds favor with God (B); God is pleased with you (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 19, Balanced and Readable give the sense; Literal keeps "grace".

source.text: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ἐκλήθητε, ὅτι καὶ Χριστὸς ἔπαθεν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν, ὑμῖν ὑπολιμπάνων ὑπογραμμὸν ἵνα ἐπακολουθήσητε τοῖς ἴχνεσιν αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: To this for you were called, because also Christ suffered for you, to you leaving an example so that you may follow the steps of him;

en.L: For to this you were called, because {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} also suffered for you, leaving you an example so that you may follow in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} steps.
en.B: It was for this that God called you, because {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} also suffered for you and left you a pattern to copy, so that you would walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} footsteps.
en.R: God called you to this kind of life, because {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} also suffered for you. He left you an example to copy, like a teacher who writes out letters for a child to trace. So follow where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} walked.

es.L: Porque para esto {{plural_you:fueron|fuisteis}} llamados, porque también {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} sufrió por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dejándo{{plural_you:les|os}} un modelo para que {{plural_you:sigan|sigáis}} de cerca {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} huellas.
es.B: Para esto Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó, porque también {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} sufrió por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:les|os}} dejó un modelo que imitar, para que {{plural_you:caminen|caminéis}} siguiendo {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pasos.
es.R: Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó a esta clase de vida, porque también {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} sufrió por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Él {{plural_you:les|os}} dejó un ejemplo para imitar, como un maestro que escribe letras para que un niño las calque. Así que {{plural_you:sigan|seguid}} el camino por donde {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} anduvo.

sw.L: Kwa maana mliitwa kwa ajili ya hili, kwa sababu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} pia aliteswa kwa ajili yenu, akiwaachieni mfano wa kunakili ili mfuatilie alama za nyayo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.B: Ni kwa ajili ya hili Mungu aliwaita, kwa sababu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} pia aliteswa kwa ajili yenu, akawaachia mfano wa kunakili, ili mtembee katika nyayo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.R: Mungu aliwaita kwa maisha ya namna hii, kwa sababu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} pia aliteswa kwa ajili yenu. Aliwaachia mfano wa kuiga, kama mwalimu anayeandika herufi ili mtoto azifuatishe. Basi fuateni njia aliyopita {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.

decisions.choice: to this you were called: to doing good and suffering patiently
decisions.reason: τοῦτο points back to verse 20. God, who called them (verse 9; 1:15), called them to a life that may include unjust suffering, as Christ's did.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "suffered"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "died" instead of ἔπαθεν ("suffered"); the same variation occurs at 3:18. "Suffered" fits the subject of these verses, which is suffering. Some manuscripts also have "for us ... leaving us" instead of "for you ... leaving you". Reviewers must check both against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: an example: a pattern to copy
decisions.reason: ὑπογραμμὸν was the model of letters a child traced over when learning to write. Christ's way of suffering is the pattern believers write over.

decisions.choice: for you: on your behalf
decisions.reason: ὑπὲρ means for someone's benefit. Christ's suffering was an example, but more than an example: it was for them, as verse 24 goes on to say.

decisions.choice: follow in his steps: walk where he walked
decisions.reason: ἴχνεσιν are footprints. To follow them is to go the way he went.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: God called you
decisions.reason: The one who calls in 1 Peter is God (m1); Balanced and Readable name him.

decisions.choice: like a teacher who writes out letters for a child to trace
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture in the word (m3).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: Spanish puts the article before "Mesías" but not before "Cristo", so the span takes it in.

source.text: ὃς ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἐποίησεν οὐδὲ εὑρέθη δόλος ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: who sin not did nor was found deceit in the mouth of him;

en.L: He did not commit sin, nor was deceit found in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth.
en.B: He never sinned, and no one ever found deceit in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth.
en.R: He never sinned. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} never lied or tried to deceive anyone.

es.L: Él no cometió pecado, ni se halló engaño en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca.
es.B: Nunca pecó, y nadie encontró jamás engaño en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca.
es.R: Nunca pecó. Y nunca mintió ni trató de engañar a nadie.

sw.L: Hakufanya dhambi, wala udanganyifu haukupatikana katika kinywa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}.
sw.B: Hakutenda dhambi kamwe, na hakuna mtu aliyekuta udanganyifu katika kinywa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}.
sw.R: Hakutenda dhambi hata kidogo. Wala hakusema uongo, wala hakujaribu kumdanganya mtu yeyote.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 53:9, about the suffering servant of the Lord
decisions.reason: Isaiah 52:13-53:12 describes the servant of the Lord who suffers for the sins of others. Peter uses its words in verses 22-25 to describe Jesus. Verse 22 follows the Greek of Isaiah 53:9 closely, with "sin" where that translation has "lawlessness".

decisions.choice: who: Christ (verse 21)
decisions.reason: ὃς begins the first of three statements about Christ (verses 22, 23, 24). The SBLGNT punctuation makes each its own sentence.

decisions.choice: deceit: lies and trickery
decisions.reason: δόλος is the same word as in verse 1. Christ is the pattern of what the readers are to put away.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}
decisions.reason: Pronoun for Christ. A sentence starting with "He" has no span.

source.text: ὃς λοιδορούμενος οὐκ ἀντελοιδόρει, πάσχων οὐκ ἠπείλει, παρεδίδου δὲ τῷ κρίνοντι δικαίως·

records.literal_gloss: who being reviled not reviled in return, suffering not threatened, kept handing over however to the [one] judging justly;

en.L: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was reviled, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not revile in return; when suffering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not threaten, but kept handing [{{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}] over to the one who judges justly.
en.B: People heaped abuse on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not answer abuse with abuse. As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} suffered, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made no threats, but went on handing {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} over to the God who judges justly.
en.R: When people insulted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not insult them back. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} suffered, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not threaten to pay them back. Instead, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept putting {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} into the hands of God, who always judges fairly.

es.L: Siendo injuriado, no injuriaba a su vez; padeciendo, no amenazaba, sino que se iba entregando al que juzga justamente.
es.B: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} cubrían de insultos, no respondía con insultos. Mientras sufría, no profería amenazas, sino que seguía poniéndose en manos del Dios que juzga con justicia.
es.R: Cuando la gente {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} insultaba, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no les devolvía el insulto. Cuando sufría, no amenazaba con vengarse. Al contrario, seguía poniéndose en manos de Dios, que siempre juzga con justicia.

sw.L: Akitukanwa, hakujibu kwa matusi; akiteswa, hakutisha, bali aliendelea kujikabidhi kwa yule anayehukumu kwa haki.
sw.B: Watu walipomtukana, hakujibu matusi kwa matusi. Alipoteswa, hakutoa vitisho, bali aliendelea kujikabidhi kwa Mungu anayehukumu kwa haki.
